name: @prized/sandbox-mcp

tools.name: create_sandbox
tools.description: Create a Prized sandbox: an isolated Linux microVM (Ubuntu 24.04) to run code in, away from this machine. Returns once it is running, usually within seconds, with the id the other tools take. Templates: prized-base-v1 (default; Python 3, Node.js 22, git, build tools) or prized-agent-v1 (adds Claude Code and Codex). Commands run as the user prized in /home/prized/work, with outbound internet; no sudo or apt, and Python packages go in a venv (python3 -m venv ~/.venv). It bills per second while running. By default it pauses after 15 idle minutes (memory and processes kept; the next call resumes it) and is deleted 7 days after it pauses or when its run time ends; delete it with delete_sandbox when done.

template.description: prized-base-v1 (default) or prized-agent-v1 (adds Claude Code and Codex).

vcpu.description: vCPUs, 1 to 32. Default 4 (2 on the free tier).

memory_gb.description: Memory in GB, 1 to 128. Default 8 (4 on the free tier).

max_runtime_minutes.description: Minutes of running before it is deleted; each resume starts them again (on the free tier the time left carries on). Default 1,440 (60 on the free tier), at most 10,080.

auto_pause_minutes.description: Pause after this many minutes without a command or file call. Default 15; 0 never. A background job pauses with it, so use 0 for one that must run unattended.

auto_delete_minutes.description: Delete it this many minutes after it pauses, up to 40,320 (28 days). Default 10,080 (7 days); 0 keeps a paused sandbox until you delete it.

env_vars.description: Environment variables for every command in the sandbox, such as a key the code inside needs. Prized stores them encrypted and its API never returns them; anything running in the sandbox can read them.

labels.description: Your own key/value tags, for list_sandboxes and the dashboard, at most 30. created-by=prized-sandbox-mcp and this install's prized-mcp-scope are always added; prized-mcp-scope cannot be passed.

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Run a shell command in a sandbox and return its exit code, stdout and stderr when it ends. It runs under bash -c as the user prized (no sudo), in /home/prized/work unless cwd says otherwise. A non-zero exit code is a result, not a tool error. Each stream is cut to its first 5,000 and last 15,000 characters; redirect long output to a file and read parts of it. It is killed after timeout_seconds (default 240, at most 3,600); progress is reported while it runs. For a server or a longer job, start it in the background (nohup cmd > log.txt 2>&1 &) and check on it with later commands; a sandbox with auto-pause on pauses it after the idle minutes. A paused sandbox is resumed first.

sandbox_id.description: The sandbox id (sbx_...), from create_sandbox or list_sandboxes.

command.description: The shell command, such as "python3 -m venv ~/.venv && ~/.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt && ~/.venv/bin/python app.py".

cwd.description: Working directory. Absolute, or relative to /home/prized/work; ~ is /home/prized. Default /home/prized/work.

env.description: Extra environment variables for this command only, on top of the sandbox's own.

timeout_seconds.description: Kill the command after this many seconds. Default 240, at most 3,600.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write a file in a sandbox, replacing it whole if it exists; missing parent directories are created. Content is UTF-8 text, or base64 with encoding "base64"; up to 100 MiB. Paths are absolute under /home/prized, or relative to /home/prized/work.

sandbox_id.description: The sandbox id (sbx_...), from create_sandbox or list_sandboxes.

path.description: Where to write: /home/prized/work/app.py, or app.py (relative to /home/prized/work).

content.description: The file content: text, or base64 when encoding is "base64".

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file from a sandbox. Text comes back 60,000 bytes at a time (a longer file's answer gives the offset to read on from). PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP images up to 5 MB come back as images; other binary files need encoding "base64" (up to 1 MiB). Paths are absolute under /home/prized, or relative to /home/prized/work. To list a directory, use run_command (ls -la).

sandbox_id.description: The sandbox id (sbx_...), from create_sandbox or list_sandboxes.

encoding.description: Leave out to get text (or an image); "base64" for the raw bytes of a binary file; "utf8" to force text.

offset.description: For text: the byte to read from, as the previous answer gave it. Default 0.

tools.name: list_sandboxes
tools.description: List sandboxes, newest first: id, state, template, shape, labels, and when each is deleted. Lists only the sandboxes this server made on this machine (the ones carrying this install's prized-mcp-scope label), the only ones its tools use, unless the person set PRIZED_MCP_ALL_SANDBOXES=1, which lists and opens every sandbox in the workspace.

state.description: Only sandboxes in this state, such as running or paused.

labels.description: Only sandboxes carrying every one of these labels. prized-mcp-scope cannot be passed: this server sets it.

tools.name: fork_sandbox
tools.description: Copy a running or paused sandbox into count live copies, each with the parent's disk, memory and running processes as they were at the fork, and its own id; the parent carries on. Set a machine up once (clone, install, build, start a server), then fork it to try several approaches in parallel from the same state. Returns once every copy is running. All or nothing: if one cannot start, none is kept and the error says why. One machine holds about 7 copies of the default 4 vCPU shape (more of smaller ones). Copies bill and count against quotas like any sandbox, keep the parent's auto-pause and auto-delete, and on the free tier keep its deletion time.

sandbox_id.description: The running or paused sandbox to copy.

labels.description: Labels for the copies, replacing the parent's (which they keep otherwise), at most 30. created-by=prized-sandbox-mcp and this install's prized-mcp-scope are always added; prized-mcp-scope cannot be passed.

tools.name: pause_sandbox
tools.description: Pause a sandbox and wait until it is paused. Memory and disk are kept, so every process carries on where it stopped when it resumes; only storage is billed. It is kept until it is deleted: by delete_sandbox, or by its auto-delete (7 days after pausing for sandboxes this server created, unless set otherwise). run_command and the file tools resume it.

sandbox_id.description: The sandbox id (sbx_...), from create_sandbox or list_sandboxes.

tools.name: resume_sandbox
tools.description: Resume a paused sandbox, every process where it stopped, and wait until it is running (usually under a second). run_command and the file tools resume a sandbox on their own; this wakes one ahead of time.

sandbox_id.description: The sandbox id (sbx_...), from create_sandbox or list_sandboxes.

tools.name: delete_sandbox
tools.description: Delete a sandbox for good: its disk, memory and processes are erased, with no undo. Copy out what you need first. Billing stops once it is gone.

sandbox_id.description: The sandbox id (sbx_...), from create_sandbox or list_sandboxes.

instructions: Prized Sandboxes are isolated Linux microVMs (Ubuntu 24.04) for running code away from this machine. Typical flow: create_sandbox, then run_command, write_file and read_file with the id it returns, then delete_sandbox when done. fork_sandbox copies a sandbox, memory and running processes included, into several live copies to try things in parallel from one state. The tools use only sandboxes this server made on this machine (the ones carrying this install's prized-mcp-scope label, which it sets itself); others in the workspace are left alone unless the person sets PRIZED_MCP_ALL_SANDBOXES=1. Sandboxes bill per second while running and pause themselves when idle (a call resumes them), so delete the ones you no longer need. Commands run as the user prized without sudo, in /home/prized/work, with outbound internet; nothing reaches a sandbox from outside unless someone opens one of its ports with the Prized CLI or API.
